_comment: What we could not check, in a golfer's words (docs/design/session_report_design.md §9.3 item 5,
§10 rule 7). The gate catalogue's own claim words are written for an analyst; a client report says
the same thing once, on its back page, in these. Read through gate_words_pack.h.
`gates`: one clause per catalogue id (Metrics/gate_catalogue.h) — per-swing gates and engine rules
alike — lower case, no digits, and WITHOUT ITS SUBJECT. One gate (sequence.sightedBand) refuses
several readings, so the clause is written to follow the reading's name: "when your hips turned
fastest: the face-on camera cannot time a turn while you are square to it…".
`subjects`: the reading a gate acted on (a gate record's subject), in golfer words. A metric subject
is not listed: the report uses that measure's `golferName` from the pack.
A gate with no clause gets no line in the report, rather than the analyst's words — an internal
phrase on a client document is worse than a gap the technical appendix fills. core_pack_test holds
this file to the catalogue in both directions.
Authored in the content phase and first shipped compiled into src/Coaching/report_gate_words.h;
moved here, word for word, so a studio can read and correct them in the Diagnostic Model (#60).
